*t t, tau=, to/, indecl., twenty-second letter of the Formello abecedaria, IG 14.2420 , but nineteenth of the Ion. alphabet, cf. Pl. Cra. 394b : as numeral t/ =
300 , but t'
=
300 , 000 .

t', apostroph. for te,
and.
toi is elided in Od. 1.60 , 347 , also in Aeolic verse, qe/lw ti/ t' ei)/phn
Sapph. 28
, cf. Alc. Oxy. 1788.15
ii 9 , but is joined with a)/n, a)/ra by crasis. Attic to/ , ta/ are never elided, but may suffer crasis.
ti\ or ti/ can suffer neither elision nor crasis.

ta/, v. o( , o(/, and o(/s.
v. ti/s .

drum, Hsch. ; cf.
tabulas (acc. pl.) in codd. of Seneca Ep. 6.4.4 .

= topa/zios , PHolm. 11.38 ; li/qon to\n kalou/menon taba/si<n> ib. 4.12 ; o( lego/menos taba/sis e)k th=s *ai)gu/ptou katafero/menos ib. 8.7 .

, cf. 4.85 , 8.81 , 95 . the copulative te becomes rare in later Gr.; it is found about 340 times in LXX , mostly in the Pentateuch and 1 -4 Ma., only 3 times in Ps.; in the NT it is found about 150 times in Act.Ap., 20 times in Ep.Hebr., and very rarely in the other books. In Ep. (more rarely in other dactylic verse, v. infr. 11 ) te stands in general or frequentative statements or in statements of what is well known; such statements are freq. made as justifications of a preceding particular statement or of a preceding exhortation to a particular person or persons; the sense of te thus approaches that of toi (cf. toi and te in Od. 2.276 - 7 , and cf. Il. 13.115 with 15.203 ); although associated with numerous particles and other words of particular types (v. infr.) its meaning remains independent of these and applies to the whole sentence in which it stands: ai)=ya/ te fulo/pidos pe/letai ko/ros a)nqrw/poisin
